modules_changed_in_v0_7_13: backtest.py (main-loop and fallback TIME-exit invariants now use effective_entry-based gross to match the basis tp_price/sl_price are derived from)

invariant_arithmetic_bug_root_cause.bug: Invariant compared gross_bps (computed from raw entry_price) against tp_level/sl_level, but the engine's TP/SL bar checks fire against tp_price/sl_price which are derived from effective_entry (= entry_price * (1 + slip*split/1e4)). The two scales differ by the entry-slippage offset (slippage_bps * entry_slippage_split). Result: legitimate timestop exits with raw gross slightly above tp_level but below the actual tp_price (so TP correctly didn't fire) falsely triggered the invariant.

production_failure.context: First HOLDOUT attempt for the discovery-restart Rule 1
production_failure.trade: 2026-01-05, IT sector, entry 13:30 ET (UTC 18:30), entry_price=186.77, timestop_open=187.74 at 15:50 ET
production_failure.math: effective_entry=186.91, tp_price=187.85, timestop_open=187.74 < tp_price → TP correctly didn't fire. raw_gross=51.94 bps, eff_gross=44.4 bps. v0.7.12 invariant tol=1 over tp_level=50 → 51.94 > 51 → raised. eff_gross 44.4 < tp_level 50 → would not have raised.
production_failure.interpretation: Engine correctly chose to raise rather than write a possibly-contaminated trade. The invariant was simply wrong.

invariant_arithmetic_bug_root_cause.fix_summary: Both the main-loop TIME-exit invariant and the fallback-path TIME-exit invariant now compute gross_eff_bps = (bar_price - effective_entry) / effective_entry * 10000 and compare to [-sl_level, +tp_level] (with 1 bp tolerance). Same basis as the bar-vs-tp_price/sl_price checks. Phantom detection capability preserved — large negative gross from AH-bar entries (e.g., -800 bps) still raises.
